title: KYC meaning and document checks
overview: KYC means Know Your Customer: checks used to establish and maintain customer information. Identity proof, address evidence and product-specific records can form part of the process. Requirements vary by institution and applicable jurisdiction.
procedure: For Call Sense Bank's synthetic KYC checklist, prepare a government-issued identity document, proof of address and a recent photograph for the demo branch workflow. Do not upload real documents here; an information request does not require sharing their numbers.

title: KYC status, updates and periodic review
overview: Periodic KYC review keeps customer information current. Updating one contact field does not necessarily satisfy all review requirements, and a pending document check can differ from an account restriction.
procedure: The synthetic process verifies the demo profile and asks an agent to review the recorded KYC status and missing checklist items. Complete real updates only through authenticated channels; no actual restriction is lifted by this prototype.

title: Tax-residency and FATCA information
overview: Tax-residency declarations and related reporting frameworks help institutions determine applicable reporting obligations. Their requirements depend on personal circumstances and jurisdiction; nationality, address and tax residence are not always interchangeable.
procedure: The Call Sense Bank demo routes declaration questions to a configured checklist and a human reviewer. This assistant does not infer a customer's tax status or provide tax advice; consult the relevant institution or a qualified adviser for real declarations.
